We compared the time taken to identify a misplaced label under two shelf arrangements. Arrangement A placed labels at the front edge; arrangement B placed them above the relevant shelf. Twelve participants performed one search under each arrangement, with the order alternated between participants.

The median search time was 19 seconds in arrangement A and 24 seconds in arrangement B. These results do not establish that arrangement A is superior. We calculated no uncertainty interval, and the sample consisted of staff who already knew the room.

The task involved a single deliberately misplaced label. Ordinary searching may involve several labels, unfamiliar categories, or interruptions. The results support conducting a further trial. A trial involving visitors would help determine whether the observed time difference also appears among people unfamiliar with the shelves.
